title: Measuring land surface temperature, near-infrared and short-wave infrared reflectance for estimation of water availability in vegetation
author: Holzman, Rivas, et al.

steps.title: Collect and label leaf samples
steps.instruction: In each field plot (2 soybean, 1 barley, 1 corn) walk the transect and collect 5–7 upper leaves per soybean plant and cut barley plants; select leaves from the upper part of the canopy as they best represent the surface seen by remote sensors; record the exact location every 15 m.

steps.title: Weigh fresh leaf material in field
steps.instruction: Immediately after collection, weigh each leaf sample using a portable electronic balance (model ES-1200HA, Jadever Scale Co.) with an accuracy of 0.01 g; record the fresh (actual) mass (Fw).

steps.title: Store leaves in sealed bags for transport
steps.instruction: Place each weighed leaf in a sealed plastic bag to prevent drying and transport the bags to the laboratory.

steps.title: Hydrate leaves to full turgidity in lab
steps.instruction: In the laboratory, hydrate each leaf for approximately 24 h with distilled water until the leaf reaches 100 % water content (turgid mass, Tw).

steps.title: Record laboratory reflectance spectra
steps.instruction: Arrange each hydrated leaf horizontally on a black surface to eliminate background reflectance and acquire spectra on the adaxial surface using a Spectra Vista Corporation SVC HR‑1024i spectrometer (FOV = 4°, wavelength range 0.35–2.50 µm). Use a 99 % Spectralon panel as reference to convert incident radiance to reflectance. Set the spectrometer distance to ~0.5 m from the leaf (covers ~3 cm²) and record in nadir orientation. Sampling intervals: ≤0.0033 µm at 0.7 µm, ≤0.0095 µm at 1.5 µm, ≤0.0065 µm at 2.1 µm.

steps.title: Perform progressive dehydration and weigh leaves
steps.instruction: After the hydrated measurement, expose leaves to sunlight and allow them to dry at ambient temperature; subsequently oven‑dry them at 50 °C until the dry mass (Dw) is constant. Weigh the leaves at each stage with the same balance (accuracy 0.01 g) to obtain fresh/actual masses during dehydration.

steps.title: Record field reflectance spectra along transects
steps.instruction: In the field, measure reflectance every 15 m along each transect under cloud‑free conditions between 10:30 and 16:00 local time, avoiding rapid solar radiation changes. Use the same SVC HR‑1024i spectrometer settings as in the lab (0.35–2.50 µm, FOV = 4°, reference 99 % Spectralon, distance ≈0.5 m, nadir orientation). Calculate the leaf‑water spectral index from reflectance at NIR = 0.850 µm and SWIR = 2.130 µm.

steps.title: Calibrate and measure canopy temperature in field
steps.instruction: Before temperature measurements, calibrate the handheld ST PRO Raytek thermometer (spectral range 8–14 µm, resolution 0.1 °C, range 0–50 °C, accuracy ≈0.3 °C) using an Everest black body (range 0–60 °C, accuracy 0.1 °C). Then, immediately after each spectral acquisition, hold the thermometer 0.5 m above the canopy at an angle of ~70° from the horizontal, pointing down to the leaves, and record land‑surface temperature (LST). Correct the radiometric temperature for surface emissivity ε = 0.985.

steps.title: Calculate relative water content for each sample
steps.instruction: Compute the relative water content (RWC, %) for each leaf using the formula RWC = [(Fw − Dw) / (Tw − Dw)] × 100, where Fw is the fresh/actual mass, Dw the dry mass, and Tw the turgid mass.
